description: Public-tier corpus registry. Every document is a published standard, regulation or program document; artifacts are signed so any consumer can verify them independently.
rules: Citations may come only from authority in {authoritative-apex, authoritative, authoritative-site, authoritative-delta, corroborating}; derived/reference-only/never-cite nodes may be retrieved but never cited.

authority, relevance and visibility are three axes and none stands in for another: authority is the publisher's standing and decides citability (rule 1); relevance (requirement | guidance | supporting | example) is the part the document plays and is what retrieval ranks and filters on; visibility is who may be shown it. A document of lesser relevance keeps its publisher's authority.
framework_rev=3 sources are admitted only for comparison intents.
Definitions, tokens and Operational Scope vocabularies load only from the row a term is defined in, never from a document that merely uses it.
Exactly one build of a document is current at a time; superseded builds are never-cite.
Only published text is projected into the graph; a field a row marks restricted is never emitted as a node or edge.
Pattern rows (document_number containing '{...}') are expanded to one row per instance at ingest.
Every row has a canonical publisher url; any copy held here is a copy, never the source of record.
Derived artifacts (chunks, vectors, nodes, edges) are trusted downstream only by cosign signature + SHA-256 from manifest.json.
Embedding model is pinned by file hash (embedding_model_id); a mismatch is a hard failure.

Every chunk carries normativity (requirement | guidance | example) assigned structurally from the row's normativity_map; an obligation claim in an answer must be supported by a requirement chunk; citations always display normativity.
JSON-sourced rows are primary; their PDFs verify text once and supply page numbers into chunk metadata only — page numbers are never written into the source JSON.

PDF/DOCX sources extract to canonical Markdown in full; chunking honours the row's sections.include / sections.exclude with covered_by naming the row that supplies the excluded content. A section matched by neither list is an 'unclassified section' finding, never a silent drop.

Each row declares language (expected) and language_policy; paragraph-level language identification drops or reports foreign-language paragraphs per policy, keeps low-confidence paragraphs with a flag, and never splits mixed-language paragraphs. New rows default to report-only.
